reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that UB induces a gradient of grain refinement and increased surface hardness in HEA coatings, but it does not provide any data on residual stresses, crack behavior, or performance under thermal cycling, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Ultrasonic burnishing (UB) induces severe plastic deformation in AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA coatings.
UB creates a gradient of fine grains and compressive residual stresses at the surface.
Grain refinement enhances hardness via the Hall–Petch effect.
Compressive residual stresses reduce crack initiation and propagation during thermal cycling.
These microstructural changes improve durability under cyclic thermal loading up to 900°C.
